chunks: 1673 - He said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the sadaqat of the People of the dhimmah and what is taken from their jizyah from the price of their wines, the meat of their pigs, and their carrion.

So he said: “The jizyah is due from them upon their wealth. It may be taken from them from the price of pork, or wine, and whatever they took from that, the burden of that is upon them, while its price is halal for the Muslims, who may take it as part of their jizyah.”

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: the protected non-Muslim subjects living under Muslim rule
key_terms.ثَمَنِ خُمُورِهِمْ: the price obtained from their wine
key_terms.جِزْيَتِهِمْ: their poll-tax obligation paid to the Islamic authority
key_terms.حَلَالٌ: lawful and permissible in this legal context
key_terms.صَدَقَاتِ: levies or dues mentioned in relation to the protected non-Muslim community
key_terms.لَحْمِ الْخِنْزِيرِ: pork, mentioned as a source of their wealth
key_terms.وِزْرُ: the burden or sin of the act

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for Muslims to take jizyah from the wealth of non-Muslims derived from wine and pork?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the jizyah taken from Ahl al-Dhimmah. It states that the liability for unlawful items such as wine and pork remains upon them, while the payment taken from their wealth as jizyah is halal for Muslims.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1673 - I asked Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about the alms (sadaqat) of the People of the dhimma and what is taken from their jizya, such as the price of their wine, pork, and carrion.

Imam (as) replied: "They are obligated to pay the jizya on their wealth, which can be taken from the price of pork, wine, or any such things. The burden (wizr) of these actions rests upon them, but the proceeds are lawful (halal) for Muslims to take as part of their jizya."
